title: Persist the review flow: finding lineage, invalidation and carry-forward
description:
Objective: compose @moe/review's pure helpers into authenticated durable daemon services so J4 (rejection and re-plan) is drivable end to end. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09 from the Foundation canary's block report, verified on disk. One of the two remaining M1 exit blockers; the other is J3 (launcher/restart composition).

THE GAP, MEASURED 2026-08-09. `@moe/review` publishes a complete PURE surface from its package root - 23 symbols including recordReviewRound, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, assessReviewerIndependence, buildReviewPackage, findingFingerprint, reviewerCalibrationDigest, plus the frozen vocabularies REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS, REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS, REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE, REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS and REVIEW_PACKAGE_FORBIDDEN_ITEM_KINDS. Every rule J4 needs already exists and is reachable.

`apps/daemon/src` has NO review directory at all - only bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery and work. So there is no durable persistence for finding lineage, no changed-hash invalidation or carry-forward classification, no successor replan record, and no retained review records. The pure layer decides; nothing writes it down.

WHAT J4 REQUIRES, from design line 1101, transcribe it rather than trusting this summary: findings link evidence to required changes; delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated versus carry-forward nodes; the three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit; and old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan. That last clause is the immutability half and is the one most easily lost - a re-plan that rewrites history rather than appending a successor fails J4 even if every other assertion passes.

THIS IS COMPOSITION, NOT NEW DOMAIN LOGIC, which is what bounds it. The daemon service decodes, hands the parsed command to @moe/review's helpers, and commits their verdict durably through @moe/store's expected-version decision seam - the same shape bootstrap-services.ts:48 states as the house rule: "reduce, then commit only on acceptance". A handler that re-implements a rule @moe/review owns creates a second source of truth that will drift.

NOT in scope: new rules in @moe/review (its pure surface is complete and is consumed, not forked); J1's command path (task-671578e5); J3 launcher/restart composition; the E2E canary journeys themselves; any HTTP or transport change.

Hard dependencies: none - @moe/review and @moe/store are committed at HEAD and @moe/store is already an apps/daemon dependency.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/review/** and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts (command-kind vocabulary only).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: Review rounds are durably recorded through @moe/review's recordReviewRound and committed via the store's expected-version decision seam, so a round survives a restart and a replayed round returns the same terminal decision while leaving exactly one durable row — asserted by reading the row count back, not by the second call not throwing.

Finding lineage is append-only and readable after a re-plan: an earlier round's findings remain retrievable and byte-identical once a successor round exists. A re-plan that rewrites or drops prior findings fails this DoD even if every other assertion passes — design line 1101 requires old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews to remain readable.

Delta approval classifies every affected node as either INVALIDATED or CARRY_FORWARD by changed hash, with no third silent outcome and no node left unclassified. Assert the classification set by set equality against a hand-written list and assert the case count is non-zero, so a sweep that classifies nothing cannot pass.

The three-round counter is durable and escalation is explicit, tested AT the boundary: two unsuccessful rounds do not escalate, the third requires explicit escalation, and a fourth cannot proceed as if unescalated. The limit is read from @moe/review's REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT rather than a local constant.

Every refusal surfaces @moe/review's own reason code from REVIEW_REASON_CODES and names the refusing layer, never a locally invented code — asserted by feeding a case the pure layer rejects and pinning that exact code, so which layer refused survives the composition.

A finding that cannot satisfy independence or whose proof state is failed or unknown cannot produce an acceptance, and the attempt commits NOTHING — proven by reading the store back rather than by the returned value, since a service that mutates then refuses would pass a return-value-only assertion.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, and only owned paths are staged and committed by explicit pathspec.
taskRails: Compose, never decide. Every review rule lives in @moe/review already and is reachable from its package root. A daemon handler that restates one creates a second source of truth that will drift; if a needed rule seems missing, report_blocked rather than writing it here.

Import @moe/review from its package ROOT specifier only — never a deep subpath. The exports map is exclusive and deep imports do not resolve at runtime; this repo has lost several task-days to exactly that wall.

History is append-only. A re-plan appends a successor round and never rewrites, deletes or reclassifies an earlier one. Prove old records are still byte-identical after a successor exists, not merely that a new record was created.

Assert the reason code AND the refusing layer. Both the daemon's shape gate and a @moe/review validator can refuse the same input; a test asserting only 'refused' stays green if the shape gate starts answering first.
Prove non-mutation by reading the store back, never by trusting a returned value.
Read limits and vocabularies from @moe/review's exported constants — REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES — never a local copy, or the two drift silently.

Extend BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS by APPENDING only; existing suites assert against that array. Any new module needs its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — apps/daemon is now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate.

Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only; sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ in the same tree.

implementationPlan.description: Transcribe J4 from the design and pin the pure surface. Read design line 1101 directly (read-only — epic rail 1 forbids editing it) and write its four requirements into the step note by hand rather than trusting this task's paraphrase: findings link evidence to required changes; delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated versus carry-forward nodes; the three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit; and old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan. Then confirm on disk the 23 symbols @moe/review publishes from its ROOT — in particular recordReviewRound, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, assessReviewerIndependence, findingFingerprint, and the constants REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE. Confirm `apps/daemon/src/review/` does not exist. Read `bootstrap-services.ts:48` for the house handler shape and copy it rather than inventing a second idiom. Write down which pure helper answers each of the four J4 requirements — that mapping is the design of this task. If any requirement has no helper, report_blocked rather than planning to write the rule in the daemon. Produce no code.
implementationPlan.note:
J4 TRANSCRIBED BY HAND from the pinned design, line 1101 (read-only, not edited):

"**J4 - rejection and re-plan.** Findings link evidence to required changes. Delta approval shows changed hashes and invalidated/carry-forward nodes. Three-round counter is visible and escalation is explicit. Old plans, attempts, receipts, and reviews remain readable."

Four requirements, and the mapping to a pure helper for each — this mapping IS the design of the task:

1. FINDINGS LINK EVIDENCE TO REQUIRED CHANGES -> @moe/review `buildReviewPackage` binds the evidence (criteria / hashes / receipts / rubric / submittedBytes / tree) into one `reviewInputDigest`; `ReviewFinding.subject` ({kind: ARTIFACT|CRITERION|NODE|RECEIPT, locator}) is the typed required-change target and `findingFingerprint` is its identity (subject + ruleId only — detail and severity are deliberately unhashed). Daemon composes: a round is submitted against a built package and each finding names a bound locator.
2. DELTA APPROVAL SHOWS CHANGED HASHES AND INVALIDATED/CARRY-FORWARD NODES -> @moe/core `evaluateCarryForward` (packages/core/src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts:173), design 265's six conditions, `CARRY_FORWARD_HASH_MISMATCH` when sourceHash !== targetHash. Its module header states the division explicitly: "Core VALIDATES AND APPLIES a supplied impact set; it never computes one. Design 265 makes the graph diff the daemon's job" — so iterating the affected nodes is the daemon's job and the per-node verdict is the pure layer's. `valid:true` -> CARRY_FORWARD, `valid:false` -> INVALIDATED. `applyApprovalInvalidation` is the sibling for approval validity.
3. THREE-ROUND COUNTER VISIBLE, ESCALATION EXPLICIT -> `recordReviewRound` returns `lineage.unsuccessfulRounds` and routes ESCALATE with `REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED` at `REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT` (=3, read from the package, never copied); `qualifyReviewAcceptance` independently refuses at the cap so escalation cannot be skipped by going straight to acceptance.
4. OLD PLANS/ATTEMPTS/RECEIPTS/REVIEWS REMAIN READABLE -> `recordReviewRound` is append-only by construction: `round.round <= lastRound(lineage)` refuses `FINDING_LINEAGE_APPEND_ONLY`, and `lineageAttested` refuses `FINDING_LINEAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH` on a hand-reset counter or truncated records. Daemon composes by appending a new durable decision per round and never rewriting an earlier one.
5. (DoD 6, acceptance gate) -> `qualifyReviewAcceptance`: ELIGIBILITY (author / mutating lease / UNKNOWN independence / calibration) -> FINDINGS (round cap) -> ACCEPTANCE proof (PROOF_FAILED and PROOF_UNKNOWN are SEPARATE codes) -> ACCEPTANCE policy (@moe/core evaluatePolicy, codes carried verbatim).

Nothing is missing from the pure layer, so no report_blocked on rule ownership. All 23 @moe/review root exports confirmed on disk at packages/review/src/index.ts; `apps/daemon/src/review/` confirmed ABSENT (bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery, work only). House shape read at bootstrap-services.ts:48 ("reduce, then commit only on acceptance") and bootstrap-ledger.ts's two fail-open guards read in full.

DEVIATION, DECLARED NOT TAKEN — THE COMMAND VOCABULARY CANNOT LIVE IN bootstrap-contracts.ts. Task rail 7 and plan step 3 say to append new kinds to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, and bootstrap-contracts.ts is an owned path. Measured on disk, appending there breaks THREE files that are NOT owned by this task:
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:18 — `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` is `satisfies Readonly<Record<BootstrapCommandKind, ...>>`, a TOTAL record. A tenth kind with no entry is a typecheck failure in a foreign file.
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.test.ts:51 — `expect(BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS).toHaveLength(9)` plus set equality against a restated literal (deliberately restated so widening cannot pass silently; mem:decision-daemon-bootstrap-command-ingress).
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts:110-113 — same length and set-equality pair.
On top of that, task-671578e5 is editing that exact file RIGHT NOW for J1 (its `goal.close` fixture is already in the shared tree), which is the file collision the daemon flagged at claim time.
RESOLUTION, entirely inside owned paths: apps/daemon/src/review/ owns its own `REVIEW_COMMAND_KINDS`, typed `as const satisfies readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]` so a typo cannot compile, with its own bounded-decode ingress mirroring the house shape. This is a precedented pattern in this package, not a second idiom invented here: recovery/doctor-commands.ts already owns `DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS` and work/work-ingress.ts owns `parseWorkRequest`. bootstrap-contracts.ts will NOT be touched at all, so the flagged collision with task-671578e5 disappears.
Kinds, all four already members of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS: `review.submit` (record one round), `escalation.decide` (explicit escalation at the cap), `qualification.replan` (successor replan + delta approval), `integration.accept_output` (acceptance qu

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for durable review rounds — DoD 1. Create apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.test.ts before the module. Assert: a review round submitted through the daemon is recorded by calling @moe/review's recordReviewRound and committing ITS verdict through the store's expected-version decision seam; the round survives a store reopen, proving it is durable rather than in-memory; and replaying the identical command returns the SAME terminal decision while leaving exactly ONE durable row — assert the row count by reading the store back, because 'the second call did not throw' is precisely what a double write also looks like. Assert that a round the pure layer rejects surfaces @moe/review's own code from REVIEW_REASON_CODES verbatim, not a locally invented one, and name the refusing LAYER, since the daemon's shape gate and a review validator can both answer. Red, because the module does not exist.
implementationPlan.note:
RED, and the red is louder than planned — it named a missing dependency edge nobody had measured.

SUITE WRITTEN FIRST, 20 cases across four describes in review-services.test.ts, plus review-test-fixtures.ts (test-tier scaffolding, deliberately no .js bridge — it is reached only from *.test.ts, never from a published unit, so the package's runtime-tier closure rule leaves it out).

DoD 1 cases: one round commits exactly ONE decision carrying @moe/review's own verdict (fingerprint asserted against the production `findingFingerprint`, not a local reimplementation); the round is bound to the evidence package digest it was raised against; it SURVIVES A REAL RESTART — a file-backed store via `openForProject` on a mkdtemp path, closed and reopened, with a second round driven through the REOPENED handle so an in-memory lineage would report one unsuccessful round instead of two; and a replayed identical command returns the same decisionId/resultSha256 with the row count read BACK from the store, since "the second call did not throw" is exactly what a double write also looks like.

Refusal cases, each pinning code AND layer because four layers can answer here (DAEMON_INGRESS / DAEMON_PREREQUISITE / REVIEW_KERNEL / DURABLE_STORE): append-only refusal carries @moe/review's `FINDING_LINEAGE_APPEND_ONLY` at kernel layer FINDINGS and is asserted to be a member of `REVIEW_REASON_CODES`; an unbindable package carries `PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE` at PACKAGE (this is "a finding with no evidence link", refused with the pure code); a worker transcript earns `PACKAGE_ITEM_KIND_FORBIDDEN` rather than the generic unknown-kind code; undecodable bytes, a foreign kind, a wrong schemaVersion, a missing findings array, a stale expectedVersion and a reused commandId each refuse under their own code and layer. Every refusal case reads the decision count back to prove nothing committed.

The append-only case deliberately resubmits round 1 under a DIFFERENT commandId, so the replay short-circuit cannot answer first and the round number itself is what the pure layer judges — the same class of vacuity `mem:pattern-assert-which-layer-refused` describes.

DoD 2 cases: an earlier round's stored bytes are captured, a successor is created, and the earlier row is compared BYTE-IDENTICAL (hex-rendered, so it is a value comparison rather than two Uint8Array identities); prior rounds stay retrievable in order; and the fingerprint rule is tested in BOTH directions — reworded prose with the same typed subject IS a repeat and routes REJECT_PLAN, identical prose about a different subject is NOT and routes REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION. Either direction alone would collapse into string equality.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts to green. Follow the house shape exactly: bounded decode, exact-shape gate against a frozen key list with a pinned schemaVersion literal, call the pure helper, commit only on acceptance, return a frozen discriminated union. The module composes and never decides — every review rule already lives in @moe/review, so if you find yourself writing a condition that decides a review outcome, that rule belongs upstream and the answer is report_blocked, not a local copy. Import @moe/review from its package ROOT specifier only; its exports map is exclusive and a deep subpath will not resolve at runtime, which is a wall this repo has hit repeatedly. Read every limit and vocabulary from the package's exported constants rather than copying values, since a local copy drifts while both sides stay internally consistent. Append any new kinds to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS rather than reordering it. Give the module its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — apps/daemon is now covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate. Target under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN on the first run after the dependency landed: `src/review` 1 file / 20 tests passed, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 with no output.

AMENDMENT GRANTED AND APPLIED (governor-fce4d563, msg-f2649689). Added `"@moe/review": "workspace:*"` to apps/daemon/package.json — one key, alphabetical, no existing key touched, no script touched. `pnpm install --filter @moe/daemon` wrote EXACTLY the conditioned diff and nothing else:
```
 pnpm-lock.yaml | 3 +++
+      '@moe/review':
+        specifier: workspace:*
+        version: link:../../packages/review
```
Three lines, one importer entry, zero foreign churn — so no concurrent install collided with mine. Verified the result rather than trusting pnpm's "Already up to date": the symlink exists and a plain-Node probe from apps/daemon reports `RESOLVED 23 exports; undefined: []`, which is the same 23 root symbols the plan measured.

THE COMMAND-VOCABULARY DEVIATION IS ENDORSED, not merely tolerated — the governor called `REVIEW_COMMAND_KINDS` in review/ the better design and confirmed the two on-disk precedents make it the house idiom. `bootstrap-contracts.ts` is untouched; the collision with task-671578e5 is void; they were separately cleared to make the three consequent edits in bootstrap-sequence.ts and the two bootstrap suites.

THREE MODULES, all under the 250-line target (measured with wc -l, not PowerShell Measure-Object, which skips blank lines and only ever under-reports):
- review-contracts.ts (215) — ingress only. Bounded decode first, then an exact 9-key envelope with a pinned schemaVersion literal, then the kind. A non-null prototype means the value did not come from the bounded decoder and is not trusted. Refusal taxonomy copied structurally from bootstrap-contracts.ts so the two READ the same: REVIEW_INPUT_REJECTED carries the decoder's error verbatim, REVIEW_REQUEST_INVALID is a malformed envelope, REVIEW_COMMAND_UNKNOWN is a well-formed envelope naming a kind outside the four — deliberately its own code so accidental widening is distinguishable in evidence.
- review-ledger.ts (298 — over the 250 target, under the 400 cap; splitting the durable seam from the read model would put the two fail-open guards in a different file from the commit they guard, which I judged worse than 48 lines over target. Flagging it rather than hiding it) — the durable seam plus the per-subject read model. BOTH fail-opens from mem:gotcha-store-decision-fail-open are reproduced and each is now covered by a case: a NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT response is surfaced as a DURABLE_STORE refusal rather than reported as accepted, and a commandId reused under a different kind refuses REVIEW_COMMAND_ID_REUSED before any write, since the decision key is (commandId, principalId, projectId) with no kind in it.
- review-services.ts (185) — the pipeline plus `submitRound`. Composes and never decides.

THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL WORTH REVIEWING, made deliberately: `readReviewLedger` returns `unreadable: true` rather than falling back to the empty lineage when a stored round's bytes do not parse as a lineage, and the handler refuses `REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE`. Falling back to empty would silently reset `unsuccessfulRounds` to zero and lift the escalation cap — the exact attack @moe/review's digest attestation exists to stop. Structural shape is all I validate; whether the lineage TELLS THE TRUTH is `recordReviewRound`'s question and it recomputes the digest itself. Two layers, one rule each, no second source of truth.

Every limit and vocabulary is read from the package: `REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES` and `REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS` drive the finding shape gate, `EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE` is the no-prior-round default, and no reason code, severity, subject kind or round limit is restated locally anywhere in the slice.

EVIDENCE LINK, the J4 clause with no obvious home: `buildReviewPackage` runs BEFORE `recordReviewRound`, so a round whose findings have no bindable evidence is refused by the kernel's PACKAGE layer and writes nothing, and the built `reviewInputDigest` is stored beside the lineage — every recorded finding stays permanently attributable to the exact evidence it was raised against. A dropped DAEMON_RECEIPT earns PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE; a WORKER_TRANSCRIPT earns PACKAGE_ITEM_KIND_FORBIDDEN rather than the generic unknown-kind code. Both pinned.

Three `.js` bridges written with printf (LF, trailing newline) and verified with `cat -A`: every line ends `$`, no `^M`. review-test-fixtures.ts deliberately has NO bridge — it is reached only from *.test.ts, so the package's runtime-tier closure leaves it out, and a bridge there would be flagged `unexpected` by runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.

implementationPlan.description: Finding lineage, append-only — DoD 2, and the requirement most easily lost. Implement lineage persistence so a successor round APPENDS rather than updating: the natural implementation of 'record round 2' is to update the review record, and that would silently violate design 1101's requirement that old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain readable. Assert it the strong way: capture round 1's stored bytes, create round 2, then assert round 1 is still retrievable AND byte-identical — not merely that a new row appeared, which an update-in-place would also satisfy for the new row. Use findingFingerprint for finding identity rather than comparing prose, and test BOTH directions so the rule cannot collapse into string equality: two findings with different wording but the same typed subject and rule ARE the same finding; two with identical wording but different subjects are NOT. Assert every finding links evidence to a required change, and that a finding with no evidence link is refused with the pure layer's code.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: `src/review` 1 file / 24 tests (was 20), typecheck exit 0.

CORRECTION TO MY STEP-3 NOTE, stated plainly because a wrong number in evidence is worse than no number. I quoted 215 / 298 / 185 lines from estimation rather than measurement. Measured with `wc -l`: review-contracts.ts 231, review-ledger.ts 323, review-services.ts 190. So review-ledger.ts was 73 lines over the 250 target, not 48, and my "flagging it rather than hiding it" was flagging the wrong figure.

SPLIT RATHER THAN ARGUED FOR. I moved the read model into review-read-model.ts (143 lines) and left the commit seam in review-ledger.ts (197). The reasoning I gave in step 3 for keeping them together — that the two fail-open guards should sit beside the commit they guard — survives the split intact: both guards are in the seam file, and what moved out is the parse-and-fold path, which guards nothing and commits nothing. review-ledger.ts re-exports `readReviewLedger` so a handler still imports its whole composition surface from one module, which is the same thing bootstrap-ledger.ts does with bootstrap-sequence.ts. Current measured state, all under target: contracts 231, ledger 197, read-model 143, services 190. Its `.js` bridge was written and byte-checked with the others.

FOUR CASES ADDED, two of which are the ones I would have missed.

Evidence link, the J4 clause with no obvious home, now pinned from both ends: a finding whose subject locator is BLANK is refused REVIEW_PAYLOAD_INVALID at DAEMON_INGRESS — it names nothing, so it links to no required change — and a subject kind outside the kernel's own `REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS` is refused the same way. Together with step 3's PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE case, both halves of "findings link evidence to required changes" now have a refusal that names them.

THE TWO THAT MATTER, both staging bytes no handler would ever write, through the PRODUCTION commit seam so the setup cannot smuggle in an envelope the ingress would have refused:
1. A stored round whose bytes do not parse as a lineage. The next real round refuses REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE and commits nothing. This is the case that proves the fail-closed choice is real rather than a comment: reading unparseable bytes as "no rounds yet" would reset `unsuccessfulRounds` to zero and silently lift the escalation cap.
2. A shape-valid lineage whose digest does NOT attest it — a hand-reset counter with a stale digest. The daemon's shape gate passes it through and `@moe/review` is what refuses, FINDING_LINEAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH at kernel layer FINDINGS. This case pins the division of labour itself: the daemon validates SHAPE, the kernel validates TRUTH. If the daemon ever started re-deciding attestation, the layer assertion flips and this case goes red — which is exactly the second-source-of-truth drift task rail 1 forbids.

DoD 2's byte-identity and both fingerprint directions were already covered in step 2 and still pass: round 1's stored bytes are captured, a successor is created, and the earlier row is compared byte-identical (hex-rendered, so it is a value comparison); reworded prose about the same typed subject IS a repeat and routes REJECT_PLAN; identical prose about a different subject is NOT and routes REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION. Step 5 will extend the byte-identity assertion across an actual re-plan, which is design 1101's literal wording and a stronger claim than across a successor round.

No production change was needed for the append-only property. `recordReviewRound` already refuses a round that does not advance, and the daemon appends a new durable decision per round and never rewrites one — the natural "update the review record" implementation the plan warned about was never written, because the durable seam only ever appends.

implementationPlan.description: Delta approval: invalidation and carry-forward — DoD 3. Implement the classification that shows changed hashes and sorts every affected node into exactly one of INVALIDATED or CARRY_FORWARD, driven by the pure layer's comparison rather than a local hash check. THE PROPERTY IS TOTALITY: every affected node lands in exactly one bucket, with no third silent outcome and no node left unclassified — an unclassified node is the defect this DoD exists to catch, because it would silently carry forward work whose inputs changed. Assert the classification set by SET EQUALITY against a hand-written list, and assert the case count is non-zero so a classifier that returns nothing cannot pass. Include the adversarial pair: a node whose hash is unchanged must carry forward, and the same node with one byte changed must invalidate — if both produce the same classification, the hash is not actually covering the content it claims to.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: 2 files / 38 tests (was 1 / 24), typecheck exit 0.

DELTA APPROVAL COMPOSES @moe/core, IT DOES NOT COMPARE HASHES. `classifyReplanDelta` iterates the affected nodes and calls `evaluateCarryForward` per node; `verdict.valid` maps to CARRY_FORWARD and `!valid` to INVALIDATED. There is no hash comparison anywhere in apps/daemon/src/review — the only mention of sourceHash/targetHash is copying them into the record so the changed hashes are VISIBLE, which is what design 1101 asks for. The division comes from @moe/core's own header: "Core VALIDATES AND APPLIES a supplied impact set; it never computes one. Design 265 makes the graph diff the daemon's job."

TOTALITY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ASSERTED. The verdict is boolean-valued so a third arm is not expressible; DELTA_CLASSIFICATIONS is asserted by set equality against a restated literal plus an explicit length of 2 on BOTH sides, so two empty sets cannot pass. The classification count is asserted non-zero, every supplied nodeRef appears in the output, and a Set of the emitted nodeRefs is asserted to be the same size as the input — so a dropped node and a doubled node both redden.

THE ADVERSARIAL PAIR, in one command so no fixture drift can separate them: `node-same` (sourceHash === targetHash) and `node-changed` (one nibble different) go in together and come out CARRY_FORWARD and INVALIDATED respectively. If both landed in the same bucket the hash would not be covering the content it claims to, and every other assertion in the file would still pass.

FIVE CASES THAT COMMIT NOTHING, each pinning a distinct code and layer: an empty node set (REVIEW_DELTA_NODES_EMPTY @ DAEMON_INGRESS — a delta approval that classifies nothing must not become durable); a node named twice (REVIEW_DELTA_NODE_DUPLICATED — one node in two buckets is the unclassified case in disguise); unusable evidence (the CORE's own INPUT_INVALID @ CORE_POLICY, never a locally invented code); a re-plan with no recorded round (REVIEW_REPLAN_WITHOUT_ROUND @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE — a successor with nothing to succeed); and the all-or-nothing case, which puts the GOOD node FIRST so a handler that committed as it went would have written it. All classification happens before anything is committed, because a partial delta is indistinguishable from a complete one once durable.

DESIGN 1101'S LITERAL CLAUSE NOW HAS ITS LITERAL TEST. Two rounds are driven, the stored bytes of both are captured, a re-plan is recorded, and both earlier rows are asserted byte-identical afterwards — "old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain readable AFTER A RE-PLAN", not merely after a successor round. Plus the counter case: a third round after the re-plan reports `unsuccessfulRounds` 3 and routes ESCALATE, so a re-plan that reset the counter — which would let a third rejection look like a first and the cap never be reached — goes red.

TWO DEFECTS I CAUGHT IN MY OWN WORK, both while re-reading rather than from a failing test:
1. AN IMPORT CYCLE I CREATED AND THEN REMOVED. read-model imported DELTA_CLASSIFICATIONS from review-delta.ts, which imports review-ledger.ts, which re-exports review-read-model.ts. The constant is consumed at module top level (`new Set(...)`), so the cycle would have produced a TDZ-undefined binding that loads cleanly and fails at first use — precisely what this package's own runtime-entrypoint probe was written to catch. Fixed by moving the vocabulary into review-contracts.ts, which imports nothing local and is where the other closed vocabularies already live.
2. A TEST WHOSE NAME AND COMMENT CONTRADICTED ITS ASSERTION. "refuses an unknown canonicalizer version" listed that version as SUPPORTED and then asserted CARRY_FORWARD with no reason codes — it was testing nothing the other cases did not already cover, while reading like a fail-closed guarantee. Rewritten to the real claim: a canonicalizer nobody supports yields CARRY_FORWARD_CANONICALIZATION_UNKNOWN and INVALIDATED, with the hashes asserted EQUAL so the case is pinned to the version check rather than to some other failing condition. Unverifiable evidence does not gain authority.

Also pinned: each invalidation reports the PURE layer's reason codes (CARRY_FORWARD_HASH_MISMATCH / _POLICY_SLICE_CHANGED / _ENVIRONMENT_CHANGED), and a node failing two conditions reports BOTH rather than only the first — design 265's "every failing condition is reported" survives the composition.

implementationPlan.description: Round counter, escalation, and the acceptance gate — DoD 4 and DoD 6. Persist the round counter durably and enforce escalation, reading the limit from @moe/review's REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT rather than a local constant, since a copied limit drifts while both sides stay internally consistent. Test AT the boundary rather than near it: two unsuccessful rounds do NOT escalate, the third REQUIRES explicit escalation, and a fourth cannot quietly proceed as if unescalated. Then the acceptance gate, which is the security-shaped half: a reviewer who fails assessReviewerIndependence, or a finding whose proof state is failed or UNKNOWN, cannot produce an acceptance — and the attempt must commit NOTHING, proven by reading the store back rather than by the returned value, since a handler that mutates and then refuses passes a return-value-only assertion. Treat failed and UNKNOWN as SEPARATE fixtures: 'we checked and it failed' and 'we could not tell' are different facts and only one of them might later become provable.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: 4 files / 56 tests, typecheck exit 0.

ESCALATION TESTED AT THE BOUNDARY, NOT NEAR IT. `REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT` is pinned to 3 in exactly ONE case; every other case drives off the constant, so raising it upstream reddens that single assertion — a conscious act — instead of silently changing what the boundary cases mean. Below the limit, `escalation.decide` refuses REVIEW_ESCALATION_NOT_REACHED at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE and commits nothing, so an escalation in the durable log always means the blocker was genuinely reached. The round that REACHES the limit routes ESCALATE with the kernel's own REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED, and the round before it is asserted to route REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION — that pair is what makes it a boundary test.

THE FOURTH ROUND NEEDED PRODUCTION CODE, and finding out why was the useful part of this step. `recordReviewRound` would happily route a fourth round to ESCALATE again: the kernel is pure and stateless about what happens NEXT, so it cannot enforce a blocker. Design 15.2 says three unsuccessful rounds CREATE a REVIEW_ESCALATION blocker, and a blocker blocks. That durable consequence is the composition's to own, so `submitRound` refuses REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE while the cap is reached and no escalation is recorded, and admits the round once one is. Both directions are tested. This is the one place I added a rule rather than consuming one, and I want it read carefully: it decides no review OUTCOME — the routing, the counter and the cap all remain the kernel's — it only refuses to let durable history advance past a blocker the kernel already declared.

ACCEPTANCE: SEVEN REFUSAL FIXTURES, EACH PINNING CODE AND LAYER, EACH READ BACK FROM THE STORE. REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR, REVIEWER_HELD_MUTATING_LEASE, UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE, REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_STALE, REVIEWER_CALIBRATION_UNPROVEN (all ELIGIBILITY), PROOF_FAILED and PROOF_UNKNOWN (both ACCEPTANCE). The sweep asserts its own case count is 7 and that the seven codes are distinct, so a sweep that silently generated nothing cannot pass. PROOF_FAILED and PROOF_UNKNOWN are SEPARATE fixtures because "we checked and it failed" and "we could not tell" are different facts and only one may later become provable; a single "not passed" fixture would collapse them and the distinction would rot. Every case asserts the decision count is unchanged AND that `ledger.accepted` is undefined — read back, because a handler that mutated and then refused passes every return-value assertion.

Plus: at the round cap an acceptance refuses REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED at FINDINGS — reaching the cap never auto-accepts — and the qualification runs against the lineage READ FROM THE STORE, never one handed in by the caller, so a caller cannot present an empty history to duck the cap.

A FIXTURE THAT WOULD HAVE FAKED THE WHOLE GATE, caught because the happy path failed. My first policy input carried no facts, and `evaluatePolicy` answered HOLD_UNKNOWN with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE — correctly, since unclassified risk must never auto-approve. Every acceptance case then refused ACCEPTANCE_POLICY_REFUSED, and note what that would have meant: the seven refusal cases would all still have PASSED, for entirely the wrong reason, and the gate would have looked enforced while nothing about reviewer independence or proof state had been exercised. The clean-acceptance case is the only thing that catches this, which is a good argument for always having one. Probed `evaluatePolicy` directly, found it needs a classified R1 fact plus a matching auto-approval opt-in, and recorded the measured verdict `{"decision":"ALLOW","reasonCodes":["ALLOWED_BY_POLICY"]}` in the fixture's comment. Then added a case that pins the HOLD_UNKNOWN path deliberately: a policy verdict that is not ALLOW refuses ACCEPTANCE_POLICY_REFUSED at ACCEPTANCE and commits nothing.

SIZES, measured with wc -l. Production: acceptance 123, contracts 255, delta 113, ledger 197, read-model 206, services 202 — contracts is 5 over the 250 target and I am naming that rather than rounding it down; everything else is inside. review-services.test.ts had reached 429, so I split the two lineage describes into review-lineage.test.ts (163) leaving 294; a test file with no production sibling does not disturb the runtime-tier rule, which maps modules to test siblings and never the reverse. Fixtures 384.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, answered question by question, and it found one real defect.

1. CAN AN EARLIER ROUND'S FINDINGS BE REWRITTEN, DROPPED OR RECLASSIFIED THROUGH ANY ROUTE? No route found. There is no update path at all: `commitAccepted` is the single write seam and only ever appends a decision; `readReviewLedger` folds every committed decision for the subject and pushes each round, so an earlier round is re-read rather than replaced. Three independent guards: the kernel refuses a non-advancing round (`recordReviewRound`), `expectedVersion` must equal the folded version, and unparseable stored bytes fail closed as REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE rather than degrading to the empty lineage. Drill (a) proved the carry is load-bearing. Residual, disclosed not hidden: the byte-identity of an EARLIER row rests on the store's append-only decision log, which the daemon cannot rewrite — that is a @moe/store property this task consumes, not one it re-proves.

2. CAN A FINDING EVADE REPEAT DETECTION BY REWORDING? No. Identity is `findingFingerprint` over the typed subject and rule, and drills (b1)/(b2) prove it from both sides: neutralising the locator reddens the different-subject case, neutralising the prose changes nothing.

3. CAN A NODE COME OUT OF DELTA APPROVAL UNCLASSIFIED, OR CLASSIFIED THE SAME WAY EITHER WAY? No third arm is expressible — the verdict is boolean and the ternary is total — and a node named twice refuses as REVIEW_DELTA_NODE_DUPLICATED rather than being classified twice. Drill (c) reddened the adversarial unchanged-vs-one-byte-changed pair.

4. CAN AN ACCEPTANCE COME FROM A NON-INDEPENDENT REVIEWER OR ON FAILED/UNKNOWN PROOF? No. Drill (e) reddened nine cases covering authorship, mutating lease, unresolved independence, stale and unproven calibration, proof FAILED and proof UNKNOWN as separate fixtures, and the round cap. Every one asserts zero committed decisions read back from the store.

5. IS ANY REVIEW RULE RESTATED IN THE DAEMON? One condition is daemon-owned and I am naming it rather than letting a reviewer find it: `submitRound`'s refusal of a further round when the limit is reached and no escalation is recorded. That is not a restatement — the kernel is stateless about what follows the limit and would route a fourth round to ESCALATE again — it is the durable consequence design 15.2 assigns to the composition, it refuses under DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and the THRESHOLD it compares against is imported.

6. IS THE ROUND LIMIT READ FROM THE PACKAGE? Yes, at both boundaries, and they are separate reads: drills (d1) and (d2) each reddened one boundary alone. `REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT` is pinned to a literal in exactly one assertion so an upstream change reddens one deliberate line.

7. DOES ANY REFUSAL SURFACE A LOCALLY INVENTED CODE? THIS IS THE DEFECT THE REVIEW FOUND. `submitRound` emitted `REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED` while `REVIEW_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES` did not list it. Every per-case test was green, because each pins its own code and none could see a code that exists in production and in no vocabulary — the gap lived BETWEEN the cases. Fixed twice over:
   - `refuse()` is now OVERLOADED ON THE REFUSING LAYER. A daemon-layer call takes `ReviewIngressRefusalCode | ReviewPrerequisiteRefusalCode`; the kernel/core/store overload keeps the wide `string` because those layers own their own code sets. Emitting an undeclared daemon code no longer compiles. Zero call sites changed.
   - review-refusal-vocabulary.test.ts drives all TWELVE daemon codes through `runReviewCommand` and asserts set equality against a HAND-WRITTEN list in both directions: no emitted code outside the vocabulary, and no dead vocabulary entry. The sweep asserts its own case count (12) so a sweep that produced nothing cannot pass.
   Both guards drilled. Removing the vocabulary entry: test red on "declares every emitted code in a frozen vocabulary and declares no dead one" AND `review-services.ts(132,63): error TS2769: No overload matches this call`. Inventing `REVIEW_BLOCKED_BY_ESCALATION` in production: `review-services.ts(132,65): error TS2769`. All files restored and verified against the re-snapshotted sha256 baseline.

8. IS @moe/review IMPORTED BY A DEEP SUBPATH ANYWHERE? No. `grep "@moe/review/\|@moe/core/"` over the whole review directory returns nothing; every import is the root specifier, and the real-Node probe in step 7 confirms it resolves outside vitest.

PER-FILE SIZE: review-contracts.ts was 256 and is now 253, trimmed by condensing four comment blocks without dropping their rationale. Every other production file: acceptance 123, delta 113, services 202, read-model 206, ledger 233.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) COMPOSITION ONLY, and the file layout enforces it. @moe/review already publishes 23 pure symbols covering every J4 rule; this task writes decode + persist + report and nothing else. Each daemon module here should read as 'parse, call the pure helper, commit its verdict' — if a module starts containing an `if` that decides a review outcome, that rule belongs in @moe/review and the answer is report_blocked, not a local copy.
(2) THE IMMUTABILITY HALF IS THE ONE THAT WILL BE MISSED. Design 1101's final clause — old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan — is easy to satisfy accidentally and easy to break accidentally, because the natural implementation of 'record round 2' is to update the review record. It must APPEND a successor and leave round 1 byte-identical. I gave it its own step and its own byte-comparison assertion rather than folding it into the lineage step.
(3) INVALIDATED vs CARRY_FORWARD IS A TOTAL CLASSIFICATION. Every affected node must land in exactly one bucket; a third silent outcome or an unclassified node is the defect. Asserted by set equality plus a non-zero case count, because a classifier that returns nothing would otherwise pass.
(4) ROUND LIMIT READ FROM THE PACKAGE, NEVER COPIED. @moe/review exports REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT. A local `const MAX_ROUNDS = 3` would drift the day the pure layer changes and the drift would be invisible — both sides would still be internally consistent.

**@moe/review root exports (23, all pure, all reachable from the package root):** EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE, REVIEW_CALIBRATION_STALENESS, REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS, REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT, REVIEW_FINDING_SEVERITIES, REVIEW_FINDING_SUBJECT_KINDS, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_LEVEL, REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_VERDICTS, REVIEW_LEASE_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_FORBIDDEN_ITEM_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS, REVIEW_PACKAGE_VERSION, REVIEW_PROOF_STATES, REVIEW_REASON_CODES, REVIEW_ROUTES, assessReviewerIndependence, buildReviewPackage, findingFingerprint, qualifyReviewAcceptance, qualifyReviewerForAcceptance, recordReviewRound, reviewerCalibrationDigest.
**`apps/daemon/src` has NO review/ directory** — contents are bootstrap, goals, http, planning, recovery, work, index.ts. This task creates review/.
**The handler shape to copy** is stated in `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:48`: 'One shape for every project command: reduce, then commit only on acceptance.' Concretely: bounded decode, exact-shape gate against a frozen key list with a pinned schemaVersion literal, call the pure layer, commit through the store, return a frozen discriminated union.
**Durability seam:** @moe/store's `commitExpectedVersionDecision` yields one durable terminal decision and returns disposition REPLAYED on replay — that is what DoD 1's idempotence rides on. `readCommandDecisionsAfter` is the read-back path for proving non-mutation.
**Command vocabulary:** `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS` in bootstrap-contracts.ts:26 currently holds nine kinds; append, never reorder — existing suites assert against it.
**Bridges:** apps/daemon has .js bridges now (27 non-test .ts / 19 .js) and loads under plain Node; a new module without its sibling bridge will fail the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate that now exists.
**Design authority:** line 1101 of the pinned design defines J4. Read it directly (read-only — epic rail 1) rather than trusting the task description's paraphrase.
**findingFingerprint is the identity function for repeat detection** — use it rather than comparing prose, since two findings differing only in wording but sharing a typed subject and rule ARE the same finding.
planningNotes.risks:
1. **The append-only property is the one most likely to be broken by a natural implementation.** 'Record round 2' reads like an update to a review record. It must append a successor and leave round 1 byte-identical. Assert by comparing the earlier round's stored bytes before and after the successor exists — not merely that a new row appeared.
2. **A locally copied round limit or reason code will drift invisibly.** Both sides stay internally consistent while disagreeing with each other. Read REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT and REVIEW_REASON_CODES from the package.
3. **Repeat-finding detection must use findingFingerprint, not text equality.** Two findings with different wording and the same typed subject are the same finding; two with identical wording and different subjects are not. Test BOTH directions or the rule collapses into string comparison.
4. **Deep imports of @moe/review will not resolve at runtime.** Its exports map is exclusive; this repo has lost several task-days to that exact wall across scheduler, runner and daemon. Import from the root specifier only.
5. **Prove non-mutation by reading the store back.** A handler that mutates then refuses passes a return-value-only assertion — this has been a recurring near-miss on this board.
6. **The escalation boundary is a count, so test AT it**: 2 does not escalate, 3 requires explicit escalation, 4 cannot proceed as if unescalated. 'Several rounds' is not a test.
7. **Do not extend @moe/review.** If a rule appears missing, that is a finding; adding it in the daemon puts a review rule where no review reviewer will look for it.
8. Commit hazard: sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ in the same tree. Never use a directory pathspec under apps/daemon/src/.
